description: Adds eight entries to each status-aware output pool, doubling every pool from 8 to 16 and providing game-line and real-world applicability hooks.

population.title: Operational Specialists
population.composition: People whose jobs match the real-world feature—drivers, nurses, librarians, groundskeepers, clerks, engineers, guides, or maintenance workers—control practical access.
population.roles: They understand schedules, hazards, restricted areas, and the difference between normal and genuinely unusual activity.
population.supernaturalConnection: None is required; their expertise makes bad supernatural assumptions easier to expose.
population.complication: The most knowledgeable worker is unavailable because of an ordinary staffing or safety problem.

population.title: Community Dependents
population.composition: Residents, commuters, patients, students, worshippers, customers, or visitors rely on the location's ordinary service.
population.roles: Their routines reveal which entrances, hours, services, and staff relationships actually matter.
population.supernaturalConnection: They are uninvolved, but harm to the site creates real human consequences.
population.complication: A covert investigation threatens a service the surrounding community cannot easily replace.

population.title: Line-Specific Observers
population.composition: Ordinary witnesses noticed details that matter differently to Kindred, hunters, mages, changelings, Garou, or another Changing Breed.
population.roles: Each witness reports the same event through the expectations created by the location's real-world purpose.
population.supernaturalConnection: Their testimony contains a genuine trace but no proof that the site itself is controlled.
population.complication: The active game line makes one witness seem credible while obscuring another equally important account.

population.title: Data-Trail Custodians
population.composition: A scheduler, records clerk, camera operator, dispatcher, archivist, or platform administrator controls the relevant ordinary records.
population.roles: They preserve timestamps and movement data without knowing why investigators value them.
population.supernaturalConnection: A supernatural actor appears only as an unexplained entry in a mundane system.
population.complication: Policy, privacy law, institutional loyalty, or technical failure prevents immediate access.

population.title: Embedded Cover Team
population.composition: A supernatural operator and informed mortal specialists perform legitimate work matching the location's actual purpose.
population.roles: Their real jobs give them access, plausible authority, records, equipment, and reasons to be present.
population.supernaturalConnection: The operation remains unofficial because formal recognition would expose the cover or provoke a jurisdictional dispute.
population.complication: A routine audit tests whether the team truly understands the institution it is exploiting.

population.title: Unstable Cross-Sphere Coalition
population.composition: Representatives of two supernatural perspectives and several mortal intermediaries cooperate because the real-world location serves all of them.
population.roles: Each group handles a different part of the site's mundane and supernatural operation.
population.supernaturalConnection: No single faction can safely claim the location without losing the others' expertise or provoking exposure.
population.complication: A change in the site's ordinary operation removes the compromise that held the coalition together.

population.title: Recognized Sphere Delegation
population.composition: A formally appointed custodian works with specialists whose titles and methods reflect the selected game line.
population.roles: They enforce access rules, document incidents, and translate the site's ordinary operation into supernatural policy.
population.supernaturalConnection: Their authority is valid within one sphere but may not be recognized by another.
population.complication: A visiting representative challenges whether the custodian's mandate applies to the current real-world use.

population.title: Joint-Jurisdiction Staff
population.composition: Multiple custodians, mortal administrators, and neutral service workers maintain one location under a negotiated cross-system agreement.
population.roles: Separate ledgers govern physical access, feeding, spiritual passage, evidence handling, resonance, and public safety.
population.supernaturalConnection: The location is formally recognized by more than one supernatural authority.
population.complication: The agreement does not specify which ledger controls a new feature created by recent real-world changes.

struggles.title: Conflict Over Real-World Use
struggles.stakes: The location's ordinary users may lose access, safety, employment, housing, transport, care, worship, or public space.
struggles.sides: Operators, workers, users, neighbors, regulators, and property owners disagree about what the place is for.
struggles.escalation: Supernatural attention worsens an existing human dispute without creating it.
struggles.resolutionClue: Understanding the actual service and who depends on it reveals a solution that occult investigation alone would miss.

struggles.title: Infrastructure and Access Failure
struggles.stakes: A real utility, route, service, building system, or environmental condition is failing.
struggles.sides: Maintenance staff, management, users, emergency services, and contractors prioritize different risks.
struggles.escalation: Delay closes the location or turns inconvenience into a public emergency.
struggles.resolutionClue: The site's tags, layout, and operating purpose identify the overlooked dependency.

struggles.title: False Pattern Amplification
struggles.stakes: A weak supernatural trace is being exaggerated into a claim about the entire location or community.
struggles.sides: Investigators, frightened residents, opportunists, witnesses, and actual supernatural actors benefit from different interpretations.
struggles.escalation: Public attention or faction mobilization harms innocent users and obscures the moving target.
struggles.resolutionClue: Real-world schedules, records, or geography show that the pattern only passes through the site.

struggles.title: Cross-Line Misreading
struggles.stakes: One supernatural system mistakes another sphere's trace for evidence of local ownership or hostility.
struggles.sides: The active game's faction, an outside sphere, ordinary site users, and a third party exploiting the confusion all react differently.
struggles.escalation: A reconnaissance mistake becomes a territorial or ideological confrontation.
struggles.resolutionClue: The real-world feature explains why multiple supernatural routes or resonances overlap here.

struggles.title: Unregistered Sphere Collision
struggles.stakes: Two groups actively use the same place for different supernatural purposes without a recognized agreement.
struggles.sides: Current users, an emerging claimant, mortal operators, and the authority that would regulate the dispute all have leverage.
struggles.escalation: Each side modifies the real-world operation to disadvantage the other, increasing exposure.
struggles.resolutionClue: The location's mundane function offers a division of access neither faction initially considered.

struggles.title: Operational Footprint Exposure
struggles.stakes: The supernatural operation cannot continue without manipulating deliveries, staffing, access logs, ecology, public events, or maintenance.
struggles.sides: Operators want secrecy while workers, users, inspectors, and rivals notice the accumulating pattern.
struggles.escalation: A normal disruption removes the cover and forces increasingly obvious intervention.
struggles.resolutionClue: One real-world dependency is responsible for most of the visible anomalies.

struggles.title: Jurisdictional Overlap
struggles.stakes: Several recognized authorities claim different rights over the same physical location and its supernatural layers.
struggles.sides: Custodians, neighboring domains, mortal operators, and outside inspectors cite incompatible mandates.
struggles.escalation: Routine access becomes a test case capable of changing policy across the city.
struggles.resolutionClue: The site's current real-world classification differs from the classification used when the mandates were written.

struggles.title: Doctrine Versus Local Reality
struggles.stakes: Official supernatural policy treats the site as an abstract asset while its actual operation has changed.
struggles.sides: Central authority, local custodian, mortal staff, site users, and reformers disagree about what compliance requires.
struggles.escalation: Enforcement damages the very feature the inventory was meant to preserve.
struggles.resolutionClue: Current maps, schedules, ecology, or institutional practice prove that the official model is obsolete.

adventureHooks.title: The Place Cannot Simply Close
adventureHooks.opening: Investigation or supernatural violence makes shutting the location seem like the safest option.
adventureHooks.reversal: Its actual service is essential to workers, patients, commuters, residents, students, worshippers, or the surrounding neighborhood.
adventureHooks.decision: Preserve ordinary operations under dangerous conditions, relocate the service, or accept the human cost of closure.
adventureHooks.reward: Protecting the mundane institution creates durable allies and a reliable local information network.

adventureHooks.title: A Real Emergency in the Wrong Story
adventureHooks.opening: Characters arrive expecting occult activity while a fire, outage, medical crisis, structural failure, environmental hazard, or missing person demands immediate help.
adventureHooks.reversal: The emergency is mundane, but supernatural methods could solve it at the cost of exposure.
adventureHooks.decision: Use extraordinary power, work through ordinary responders, or continue the original investigation.
adventureHooks.reward: The emergency reveals the location's true access routes, dependencies, and trustworthy personnel.

adventureHooks.title: The Correct Evidence and the Wrong Supernatural Theory
adventureHooks.opening: The location provides authentic evidence that strongly resembles the active game line's expected threat.
adventureHooks.reversal: The trace belongs to another sphere or merely crossed the site through its ordinary network.
adventureHooks.decision: Follow the unfamiliar explanation, report the expected one, or conceal uncertainty from allies demanding action.
adventureHooks.reward: Correct interpretation prevents a cross-faction incident and identifies a larger hidden route.

adventureHooks.title: The Data Knows More Than the Witnesses
adventureHooks.opening: Everyone at the site remembers an ordinary day, but schedules, transactions, sensors, ecology, or infrastructure record an impossible pattern.
adventureHooks.reversal: The pattern documents movement through the location rather than activity originating there.
adventureHooks.decision: Take the records, protect their custodians, or leave the evidence in place to capture the next passage.
adventureHooks.reward: The real-world system predicts when and where the trace will appear again.

adventureHooks.title: A Site Between Systems
adventureHooks.opening: The active game line discovers a working supernatural site designed around another sphere's assumptions.
adventureHooks.reversal: The site's ordinary function makes both interpretations useful, and neither faction can operate it alone.
adventureHooks.decision: Create a joint arrangement, seize the site, expose it to a regulator, or preserve its unofficial neutrality.
adventureHooks.reward: Cooperation unlocks a capability unavailable to either system independently.

adventureHooks.title: The Cover Depends on the Place
adventureHooks.opening: A pending renovation, closure, route change, staffing shift, or ownership transfer will destroy the supernatural operation's mundane cover.
adventureHooks.reversal: Preventing the change would harm ordinary users or require obvious manipulation.
adventureHooks.decision: Move the operation, corrupt the decision, preserve the site, or let the cover collapse.
adventureHooks.reward: A successful transition creates a cleaner and more context-aware operation elsewhere.

adventureHooks.title: The Ledgers Describe Different Places
adventureHooks.opening: Multiple supernatural authorities produce valid records for the same coordinates.
adventureHooks.reversal: Each ledger describes a different layer of the site's actual use, history, ecology, or infrastructure.
adventureHooks.decision: Choose one authority, reconcile the records, divide access, or reveal that the overlap was intentionally hidden.
adventureHooks.reward: The reconciled record becomes a map of the city's larger cross-system influence network.

adventureHooks.title: A Sphere-Specific Inspection
adventureHooks.opening: An inspector from the selected game line arrives to evaluate the site under that system's doctrine.
adventureHooks.reversal: Compliance with the inspection would violate the site's real-world obligations or another recognized supernatural mandate.
adventureHooks.decision: Stage compliance, challenge jurisdiction, expose the conflict, or change the site's operation permanently.
adventureHooks.reward: The inspector can grant a formal exception that becomes politically valuable elsewhere.

locationSeeds.title: A Civic or Neighborhood Anchor
locationSeeds.premise: The location's real-world purpose makes it socially important even without supernatural ownership.
locationSeeds.firstScene: Establish who relies on the service, route, public space, institution, or business before introducing danger.
locationSeeds.longTermUse: Track how supernatural politics alter access, staffing, trust, and neighborhood stability.

locationSeeds.title: Pressure on the Mundane System
locationSeeds.premise: A real-world process—maintenance, regulation, ecology, logistics, ownership, or public access—is already close to failure.
locationSeeds.firstScene: Characters encounter the practical problem before they understand why supernatural actors care about it.
locationSeeds.longTermUse: The site's ordinary condition becomes a recurring campaign clock independent of supernatural plots.

locationSeeds.title: Context Without Ownership
locationSeeds.premise: The location repeatedly provides clues because of its geography or operation, yet no supernatural group controls it.
locationSeeds.firstScene: A clue makes sense only after the characters understand the site's actual timetable, users, environment, or records.
locationSeeds.longTermUse: The place becomes a neutral reference point that different factions interpret through their own game-line assumptions.

locationSeeds.title: The Real-World Pattern Is the Clue
locationSeeds.premise: Supernatural movement can be inferred from ordinary deliveries, tides, transit, staffing, school terms, events, or maintenance cycles.
locationSeeds.firstScene: The characters initially dismiss a mundane pattern that later predicts the next incident.
locationSeeds.longTermUse: Each return adds another data point and makes the site a valuable but vulnerable observatory.

locationSeeds.title: System-Specific Emergence
locationSeeds.premise: The location's real-world operation accidentally creates a useful effect best understood through the selected game line.
locationSeeds.firstScene: A routine change makes the effect repeatable enough for a faction to notice.
locationSeeds.longTermUse: Track whether the site becomes a haven, locus, Mystery, freehold, hunter asset, or contested hybrid.

locationSeeds.title: Unified Collision Point
locationSeeds.premise: Several supernatural systems independently exploit different aspects of one real-world location.
locationSeeds.firstScene: The characters discover that an apparent single-faction operation is actually a fragile layered arrangement.
locationSeeds.longTermUse: The site becomes a laboratory for alliances, misinterpretations, shared infrastructure, and escalating jurisdiction.

locationSeeds.title: Recognized Local Nexus
locationSeeds.premise: The site's real-world function makes it too useful, visible, or dangerous to remain outside formal supernatural administration.
locationSeeds.firstScene: Characters encounter an access protocol built around both mundane policy and the selected game line's authority.
locationSeeds.longTermUse: Changes in the real institution repeatedly force revisions to supernatural law and custodianship.

locationSeeds.title: Layered Jurisdiction
locationSeeds.premise: Several supernatural authorities formally recognize different functions of the same place.
locationSeeds.firstScene: A simple request requires permissions from incompatible custodians.
locationSeeds.longTermUse: The location becomes a recurring political map of cross-system treaties, loopholes, and unresolved borders.

items.title: Site-Specific Access Record
items.appearance: A sign-in sheet, appointment list, transit manifest, room booking, permit, key log, trail register, or maintenance access record appropriate to the location.
items.function: It establishes who could legitimately enter and when.
items.hiddenValue: A small procedural exception identifies the route used by someone avoiding normal access.

items.title: Operational Dependency Map
items.appearance: A floor plan, utility diagram, service map, route chart, ecological survey, evacuation plan, or staff-created sketch.
items.function: It shows how the real-world location continues to operate.
items.hiddenValue: One dependency also explains the apparent supernatural pattern without making the site supernatural.

items.title: Cross-System Evidence Fragment
items.appearance: An ordinary photograph, ticket, map annotation, damaged object, environmental sample, or witness recording contains details meaningful to more than one supernatural system.
items.function: It proves that something unusual crossed the site.
items.hiddenValue: Different game lines extract different truths, and combining them reveals the direction of travel.

items.title: Environmental Trace Container
items.appearance: A maintenance sample, water bottle, soil bag, air filter, medical specimen, discarded food package, or evidence envelope was collected for an ordinary reason.
items.function: It preserves a short-lived physical or resonant trace.
items.hiddenValue: The trace matches another location connected through real infrastructure or ecology.

items.title: Line-Bound Working Tool
items.appearance: Ordinary equipment has been adapted according to the selected game line: feeding logistics, spirit practice, hunter surveillance, oneiromancy, occult instrumentation, or species-specific access.
items.function: It converts the location's real-world operation into a repeatable supernatural advantage.
items.hiddenValue: Its design reveals the operator's assumptions and the sphere they expected to confront.

items.title: Improvised Shared Protocol
items.appearance: A hybrid checklist, code phrase, access marker, ritual sequence, route plan, or equipment modification combines methods from several supernatural systems.
items.function: It allows incompatible users to share the site without formal recognition.
items.hiddenValue: One step was added after a previous alliance failed and identifies the absent participant.

items.title: Sphere Credential Set
items.appearance: A badge, seal, writ, token, encoded invitation, spirit mark, compact, or ritual proof is paired with ordinary institutional identification.
items.function: It authorizes access under the selected game line's rules and the site's mundane procedures.
items.hiddenValue: The supernatural credential and mundane identification expire under different conditions.

items.title: Multi-System Jurisdiction Dossier
items.appearance: A secured file combines property records, maps, ecological surveys, supernatural claims, access agreements, incident reports, and contradictory annotations.
items.function: It documents how several authorities divide the location's physical and supernatural layers.
items.hiddenValue: One apparently mundane map revision quietly transfers control of an entire influence corridor.
